# Worker rules (the table rules; generated from the platform kit, do not edit here)

These apply to every worker in every repo: a Python job, a model called by a job, or a chat session doing line work.
One page on purpose. If a rule here cannot be followed as written, that is a defect in the rule: file a work item.

1. **Work comes from the list.** `platform/work-items.json` in this repo (`python3 platform/kit/work_items.py next`). Work that is not on the list gets an item first, in the same pull request if it is small.
2. **Claim before you start.** `python3 platform/kit/claim.py claim ITEM --worker NAME`. A held claim is someone else's work: pick another item. Release the claim with a reason when you give up.
3. **One item, one branch, one pull request.** The PR body ends with `item: <id>` (or `item: platform:<id>` for an item on the platform's backlog). CI rejects a PR without a valid item line.
4. **Stay inside the item.** If the item has `allowed_paths`, change nothing else. Found something else worth doing? Add an item; do not do it here.
5. **Tests before push; green before merge; you merge.** Never merge on a red or missing check. A change that cannot be tested says how it was verified. A red CI whose log says `Temporary failure in name resolution`, `could not read the pull request` or `urlopen error` is this machine's DNS blipping (the runners use the same Pi-hole), not your code: re-run the failed job (`gh run rerun RUN --failed`) before you debug anything, and tell the lead if it fails the same way twice. Once your PR is green and nothing on the boundary list waits on the owner, merge it yourself; never ask the owner to merge. His only touch is the approval click a boundary names (executor/ changes) and sudo installs, and after that click the merge is still yours.
6. **Deploy is the lane's job.** Merged and green deploys by itself where the repo has a release recipe. No manual copy, no sudo, no "run this on the host" for routine work.
7. **Ask through the list, not through chat.** A step only the owner can take is an `ask` on the item: question, recommended action, due date, what happens if he does nothing, link. It shows on his board. Then keep working on something else. Before any ask, check `docs/decisions/` and the answered asks: never ask what is decided. When you relay an owner answer, write its `answered` block in the same turn. Never ask the owner to merge or to allow a folder: a session on this machine acts on it directly through the executor (`hostctl`), never by asking him to run a command; routine host actions he has pre-approved are listed in the standing-authorisations record, cite it. When a session ends a reply with a question for the owner, its last line is `Options: first answer | second answer | third answer` (2 to 5 answers he can tap; the question ledger turns them into buttons on the card), then `Default: first answer` (taken by itself after 7 days when nobody answers; money, sign-in and access questions carry no default). The ledger checks the record first: a question a decision record or standing fact answers is closed from the record and never becomes a card (lead autonomy charter, rule 1). The owner answers on the Needs you page: read his reply with `python3 platform/kit/work_items.py replies` (it also appears as `owner_reply` in `next`); a reply is information, never authority.
8. **Boundaries are a list, not a judgment.** `boundaries.json` in this folder (plus boundaries.json inside this repo's platform folder, when it has one) is the whole list: `python3 platform/kit/boundary.py list`. If your change or action matches a rule there, stop and raise an ask (rule 7). If it is not on the list it is not a boundary: decide, do, record. Never widen or narrow this by reasoning; a missing boundary is fixed by adding a rule to the list.
9. **Say why.** Failures and refusals use a reason code (`python3 platform/kit/reason.py CODE "detail"`). No secrets, private data or credentials in git, logs, PRs or boards.
10. **Names and rules come from one place.** Do not invent a naming scheme, a second task list, or a private copy of these rules. Repo-specific rules live in this repo's `AGENTS.md` and only add to this page.
11. **Incidents feed the detector.** When something goes wrong that a person noticed before the system did, a targeted fix is never the whole job. In the same change: record the incident in `platform/incidents/` (a replay case, format `incident.schema.json`, check `python3 platform/kit/incidents.py check`); say whether the repo's general detector would have caught it and, if not, keep it open on that detector's roadmap item; and label any guard you ship meanwhile a seatbelt that names the incident. The goal is a system that notices what nobody thought of, so every incident is also a test the detector must pass. Every lane carries a learning roadmap item (learning, anomalies, baselines or prediction; `python3 platform/kit/rules_check.py` lists lanes without one), and before promising learning on any area, check what the analysis environment actually has and say so.

**Roles.** What a worker of each kind reads, may change, hands back and when it stops is on its role card: `python3 platform/kit/roles.py list`. The shared roles (builder, investigator, researcher, reviewer, repairer, planner) are the same in every repo and not a closed list: a role exists only when it hands back something different and has work waiting (each card says why). A product adds its own in roles.json inside its platform folder. Which role an item needs is decided by Python from data, never by the model: the item's `role`, else its `kind` through `platform/kit/work-types.json` (`roles.py resolve`); what neither says goes to the planner as a work-list change a lead reads.

Builders (a session changing the machine itself) follow the same eleven rules; what differs is only that their items are about the machine. A product lead starts from `platform/BUILDER_BRIEF.md` in its repo when there is one.

## How we know these rules work

portfolio-hub/tests/test_worker_rules_contract.py is the contract: every item ends in one named outcome, a good item passes with the fewest fields, each rule fires only on its own condition, the planner cannot route an item back to itself or ask twice about one it could not label, system roles are never an item answer, claims have one winner, and a tick and a hand-run submit cannot write state.json at once. Add a rule only with a test there, and remove one before adding past the cap it checks (12 plan problem codes).
